title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: 1986 notes (chapter IX, 'Ateliers'). Σ is a 'spectre', apparently a lattice-like structure with sup, a least element ∅_Σ and some notion of disjointness. Figopt(Σ) and Figoptdisc(Σ) are families of 'figures' in Σ. The relation ≪ between families is a refinement-type relation; the previous page builds it from a flag F_0 ≪ … ≪ F_n in some (F, ≪). The aim is to state an axiom ('Axiome … 3', given on the next page) saying that every such flag yields a family of mutually compatible elements.

Definition (completed from the previous page). A family A ⊂ Σ is 'commensurable in the set-theoretic sense' (later 'admissible', then 'commutable') if A ⊂ Σ' for some Σ' ⊂ Σ stable under sup (and presumably inf) that is a Boolean algebra. In other words, A sits inside a Boolean sub-structure, a 'Boolean block'.

Grothendieck notes this is stronger than pairwise commensurability. A chain A_0 ≪ A_1 ≪ … ≪ A_n is called commensurable if the union of the A_i is.

Lemma 3 (a disjointification of a flag):
- For each i ≥ 1 and each a_i ∈ A_i, take a''_i from Lemma 2 (not visible) for the step A_{i-1} ≪ A_i. Presumably a''_i is the part of a_i 'new' with respect to A_{i-1}, something like a_i minus the sup of the elements of A_{i-1} below it.
- Put A''_i = {a''_i ≠ ∅}, A''_0 = A_0, and A'' = ⋃_{0≤i≤n} A''_i.
- Claims (finished on the next page): each A''_i consists of nonzero mutually disjoint elements; the A''_i are mutually disjoint from one another; and the flag (A_i) is commutable iff A'' is.

So compatibility of a whole flag is reduced to compatibility of one family of pairwise disjoint 'atoms' extracted from it, much like orthogonalising a flag of subspaces into successive orthogonal complements. This criterion is nontrivial in a general lattice. Pairwise-disjoint elements need not lie in a Boolean sublattice: the three atoms of the diamond lattice M3 are pairwise disjoint and generate a non-distributive sublattice. The vocabulary ('spectre', 'commensurable', 'commutable', Boolean subalgebra containing a family) is exactly that of compatibility and Boolean blocks in quantum-logic / orthomodular lattices.
errors: The first union defining commensurability of the chain is written over 1≤i≤n; it should presumably run over 0≤i≤n (A_0 is included later).
The disjointified union is called A, clashing with A = ⋃A_i above; it should be A''. The next page then reuses 'A' ambiguously.

The equivalence 'flag commutable ⇔ A'' commutable' needs two things. First, a''_i must be expressible by Boolean operations inside any Boolean Σ' containing A, i.e. relative complements in Σ' must agree with those used in Lemma 2 in Σ. Second, each a_i must be recoverable as a sup of elements of A''. Neither is checked on this page; both depend on Lemma 2 and on the axioms on Σ, which are not visible.

The remark that commensurability is stronger than pairwise commensurability is correct for general lattices. It fails in orthomodular lattices, where pairwise compatible families always lie in a Boolean block, so the intended class of Σ matters.

ideas.what: A family of elements of a lattice-like 'spectrum' is 'commensurable/commutable' if it lies in a sub-structure stable under sup which is a Boolean algebra; this is strictly stronger than pairwise commensurability.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility / commutativity of elements in quantum logics; Boolean blocks (maximal Boolean subalgebras) of orthomodular lattices or posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936); Foulis, Holland, Kalmbach, Greechie (1960s–80s) for compatibility and blocks in orthomodular lattices

ideas.what: Lemma 3: disjointification of a flag A_0 ≪ … ≪ A_n into successive 'new parts' a''_i, giving a family of pairwise disjoint nonzero elements whose commensurability is equivalent to that of the flag.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonalisation of a flag / successive relative complements (Gram–Schmidt analogue in a lattice); reduction of compatibility to a disjoint family
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique (e.g. in orthomodular lattice theory and measure/partition refinement)

ideas.what: An axiom requiring that every flag of 'figures' induce a commutable flag of discrete spatial figures in Σ_A (completed on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility (commutativity) axiom for refinement flags; akin to requiring that chains of propositions/projections commute

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'spectrum' Σ of spatial figures whose key condition is exactly the quantum-logic notion of a commuting (compatible) family contained in a Boolean block. He explicitly renames 'admissible' to 'commutable' and stresses that the condition is stronger than pairwise. This is an undocumented contact of his late foundational work on spatial figures with orthomodular-lattice / quantum-logic ideas; the specific Σ and the purpose of the 'Ateliers' notes would need the surrounding pages to confirm.
missed.quote: les a ∈ A sont "commensurables dans le sens ensembliste" (NB c'est plus fort que d'exiger qu'ils le soient 2:2), si A ⊂ Σ', … qui est une alg. de Boole
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's late interest in noncommutative/'commensurability' structures on lattices of spatial figures. This is relevant to historians tracing his views on the continuum and physics, and possibly to Bohr-topos / Boolean-context approaches.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary: a Boolean-subalgebra compatibility condition and a disjointification lemma. The mildly notable part is the context: an unpublished 1986 axiomatics of 'spatial figures' using quantum-logic-style commutability, which seems absent from the literature on Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'des [?]' before the chain A_0 ≪ … ≪ A_n most likely reads 'drapeau', i.e. 'étant donné un drapeau', consistent with the previous page.
The insertion over 'élément' reads 'non nuls': 'formés d'éléments non nuls mut. disj.'.
The second union should be read as defining A'' (over 0≤i≤n); the manuscript letter is A with a crossed-out 'et' before it.
'Lemme 3]' is preceded by a crossed/underlined bracket mark, and the struck line above reads approximately 'On pourrait … l'exp[ression]'.
'Σ' un φ "sous-ensemble"' is uncertain; it is possibly 'Σ' un sous-"sous-ensemble"' or 'sous-algèbre', and the meaning (a sub-structure stable by sup which is Boolean) is clear.
